name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,412

clue.text: Ascot, say, in which new race unfolded around back of paddock

indicators.note: something unfolded is opened out and rearranged, so the letters lose their printed order
the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept
the shuffled letters go around another piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: both words taken as written, to be shuffled
the final letter of paddock

explanation.surface: A race meeting at Ascot where a fresh race got under way around the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot reads as the Berkshire racecourse, which the paddock supports, but here an ascot is a broad cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide tie or cravat worn around the throat, one example of clothing for that part of the body.

clue.text: Online friend entering part of the UK, Asian national

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so the friend sits inside the region

blocks.note: NI is Northern Ireland
an e-pal is a friend met over the internet

explanation.surface: An internet pen friend moving to a corner of Britain turns out to be from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a citizen of Nepal, the Himalayan country in South Asia.

clue.text: A circle supporting clubs to do with welfare

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the words before it go below the clubs

blocks.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
taken as written
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A circle of people backing local clubs in the name of community welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts A and the circle beneath the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring professions and caring work are concerned with looking after people's wellbeing and needs.

clue.text: Wit leaves deranged modern worker?

indicators.note: deranged literally means put out of order, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: a wag is a witty joker
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A joker storms out of the office in a rage, fed up with modern working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb about the wit walking out; it is the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage slave is someone wholly dependent on a salary, a jokey image of today's employee; the question mark flags the humour.

clue.text: Deny validity to a Greek character in the Netherlands

indicators.note: in places the letter and the Greek character inside the country's code

blocks.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands
taken as written
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek resident in Holland having their legal status questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it void, refusing it any legal force.

clue.text: Conflict kept us sleepless essentially

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the phrase, where the answer sits inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of kept, all of us and the start of sleepless

explanation.surface: A quarrel that kept the household awake all night.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous struggle or scuffle, a small-scale fight or dispute.

clue.text: Custom in Prohibition?

blocks.note: first meaning: habitual practice
second reading: Prohibition was an era in America

explanation.surface: A tradition that survived the ban on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Prohibition, the 1920s ban on alcohol, was an American age; split the answer as US AGE, with the question mark flagging the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means customary practice, the habitual way something is done, as in common language usage.

clue.text: Director interrupting a certain young man is weighty figure

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another thing

blocks.note: some can mean a certain, as in some person
a boy is a young male
D is a standard abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A film director cutting in on a young man who turns out to be an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a somebody means they are an important or influential person, as opposed to a nobody.

clue.text: Risk in marriage counsellor's suggestion?

blocks.note: first meaning: to put in danger
second reading: advice to stop being cross, split into two words

explanation.surface: Something risky in what a relationship adviser recommends.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as END ANGER, just what a counsellor might advise a feuding couple; the question mark marks the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to expose it to harm, which is to risk or jeopardise it.

clue.text: Intimate in Paris exotic parts first in seasoned food

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A close friend in Paris samples exotic spiced dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' says the rearranged letters come before the French friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured beef seasoned with garlic, pepper and spices, then smoked.

clue.text: Pressure put on a newspaper concerning model

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
taken as written
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A tabloid being pressured over a story about a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example to follow, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Weapon smuggled in dodgy deal making one this?

definitions.note: the whole clue's scene supplies the sense: frightened

indicators.note: a dodgy deal is unsound and crooked, so its letters are bent out of order
goods smuggled in are hidden inside something else

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A gun slipped across in a shady arms deal would leave anyone frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: a weapon smuggled in a dodgy deal makes one scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alarmed is feeling sudden fear or anxiety, the natural reaction to discovering a hidden gun.

clue.text: Old school punishment is a reflection of age

blocks.note: first meaning: sentences a pupil had to copy out repeatedly
second meaning: wrinkles seen on an older face in the mirror

explanation.surface: Remembering a traditional classroom penalty makes you feel your years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' hints at seeing creases in the mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils were given lines to write as a penalty, and lines on the face are wrinkles that come with getting older.

clue.text: A lot of young brats initially favoured place for rejects?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together
the first letter of brats
in means fashionable or in favour

explanation.surface: Spoilt kids being preferred over everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter bin is a public receptacle for rubbish, where unwanted things are thrown away; the question mark softens 'rejects'.

clue.text: Journalist observed part of ship without leader in war film

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist, often a jobbing one
saw means observed
the bridge is where a ship is steered from

explanation.surface: A war correspondent watched part of a ship lose its commander in a battle movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacksaw Ridge is Mel Gibson's 2016 film about a conscientious objector serving as a medic at Okinawa.

clue.text: Illegal practice in pass to a goalkeeper?

blocks.note: first meaning: a bribe or secret payment
second reading: a footballer booting the ball backwards to the keeper

explanation.surface: A football back-pass is against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football's back-pass rule; the question mark flags a literal reading of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickback is an illicit payment made in return for a favour, a form of corrupt bribery.

clue.text: Dissident free to move round America raised family

indicators.note: letters made to move change places, giving a new order
the rearranged letters go round the country, enclosing it
in a down clue, raised means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
US is the United States
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A dissenter, allowed to leave, travels around the States after bringing up a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised family' reads as having brought up children; in a down clue it turns the family word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuseniks were Soviet Jews denied exit visas, and by extension the word means anyone refusing to comply in protest.

clue.text: Broadcaster lacking gravity is opening in building

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
light means lacking weight or seriousness

explanation.surface: A frivolous TV channel opens a new building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' reads as solemnity, but in the setter's reading a light thing lacks weight in either sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A skylight is a window set into a roof, an opening that lets daylight into a building.

clue.text: Stimulating attribute in queen entering good French city first off

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed from the city
the royal abbreviation goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, hence good
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: A queen's arrival in a French city was the exciting attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen abbreviation goes between good and the headless city.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquancy is a pleasantly sharp or stimulating quality, of flavour or of interest.

clue.text: I face shrieks becoming wild for musical group

indicators.note: letters becoming wild run riot and settle in a new order

blocks.note: all three words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer faces screaming fans going wild at a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser Chiefs are a Leeds indie rock band, known for songs like I Predict a Riot and Ruby.

clue.text: Use a lot of milk sloppily as breakfast fare

indicators.note: a lot of but not all, so the final letter is dropped
done sloppily means done carelessly, leaving the letters in a mess

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Pouring too much milk messily over the morning cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, typically eaten in the morning with milk.

clue.text: Remoteness inspector denied in attitude

indicators.note: something denied is withheld, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: distance is remoteness
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective refused promotion becomes aloof in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a mental position or standpoint on a matter, an attitude or point of view.

clue.text: No good English graduate wearing scowl in part of pub

indicators.note: the pieces wear the scowl like a garment, so the scowl wraps around them

blocks.note: to lour is to frown or scowl
NG is the abbreviation for no good
E is short for English
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A useless English graduate frowning in the corner of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a British pub, as opposed to the public bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional British pubs were divided into rooms, and the lounge bar was the smarter, carpeted section.

clue.text: Nothing to trumpet on reflection for screen icon

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: O is a zero, nothing
to trumpet is to boast or brag

explanation.surface: A modest film star with nothing to boast about, after some thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star of the 1920s and 30s, a legend of the cinema.

clue.text: Show survey in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as the word sounds when spoken, not as spelt

blocks.note: a review is a survey or appraisal

explanation.surface: Showing the results of a survey at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical show of sketches, songs and dances, often satirical.

clue.text: Sport reduced by a third with introduction of this gym exercise

indicators.note: cut by a third, so two of the six letters are lost from the end
an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: squash is a racket sport
the first letter of this

explanation.surface: Cutting back on a sport in favour of working out at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A squat is a strength exercise in which you bend at the knees and hips, then stand back up.

clue.text: Kelly and Morecambe, perhaps, overlapping of a kind?

indicators.note: names that overlap share a letter, so one copy of it is dropped where they meet

blocks.note: Gene Kelly was the star of Singin' in the Rain
Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A Hollywood dancer and a British comic who share some resemblance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that the two surnames stand for first names; Gene and Eric share an E where they join.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means relating to a whole class or kind of things rather than a specific one; the question mark admits a loose fit.

clue.text: Meat cooked in ovens

indicators.note: food that is cooked is transformed, so the letters are reworked too

blocks.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Meat being roasted in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the meat of deer, a game meat often roasted or stewed.

clue.text: Gadget to follow diminutive pet

blocks.note: a toy can be a gadget or trinket
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A device designed to track a small pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy breeds such as the Chihuahua are very small companion animals kept as pets.

clue.text: Accessory found in enclosure, retired English rogue

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
fink is slang for a contemptible person or informer
E is short for English

explanation.surface: A useful item turned up in a pen belonging to a retired English villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A penknife is a small folding pocket knife, a handy everyday item carried around.
